## Context
Two clean `make test` runs while implementing story 4e3e-d36f-53b9-4c1e each completed 8,906 tests successfully and failed only `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py::test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict`: `caplog.records` contained no `llm call [` INFO record. The node passes in isolation, its full module passes 12/12, and the immediately preceding module plus it pass 21/21. This demonstrates a broader full-suite order/global-logging-state leak unrelated to bridge-fsck.

## Approach
- Reproduce with a minimized ordered prefix of the full collection and identify the earlier test or fixture that mutates logger level, propagation, handlers, disable state, or capture integration without restoring it.
- Fix the leaking test/fixture or make the telemetry contract robust at the correct boundary; do not weaken the assertion merely to hide global state.
- Add a regression that fails when the contaminating test and telemetry test run in the proven order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A minimized deterministic test order reproduces the missing INFO capture before the fix and passes after it.
- [x] The responsible logger/capture global state is restored between tests, with a regression proving isolation.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` passes alone, after the contaminating test, and in the complete non-integration suite.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Evidence
Both full-suite failures and focused pass counts are recorded on discovered-from story 4e3e-d36f-53b9-4c1e.
